DESKTOP TOOL PRIVACY NOTICE

Twilock Slideshow Inbox privacy

This notice applies to Twilock Slideshow Inbox, the internal desktop tool operated by Hussain Taheri. The separate Twilock iPhone app is described in its own privacy policy.

TikTok account data

With the account owner’s consent, TikTok Login Kit returns an account identifier, username, display name, authorized scopes, access token and refresh token. The tool uses these to verify the intended account and upload only the reviewed draft the operator requests. TikTok credentials are entered on TikTok’s own pages; the queue does not receive the account’s password.

The requested scopes are user.info.basic, user.info.profile and video.upload. The tool requests the exact username, display name and account identifier; it does not use the profile scope to collect a biography or verification status.

Local storage

App credentials, account tokens, draft copy, original ordered slide snapshots and TikTok upload receipts are saved in a private local directory on the operator’s Mac. The tool restricts access through filesystem permissions and a local session. It does not run a cloud account database and does not send its queue data to the Twilock iPhone app’s analytics or advertising services.

When data is sent elsewhere

The app key, secret and authorization data are sent to TikTok’s official endpoints to authorize or refresh the account connection. For a requested draft upload, the selected title, description and public JPEG URLs are sent to TikTok. TikTok downloads the images and provides upload status; the user completes editing and posting in TikTok.

The operator deploys approved JPEGs to the owned image host. These URLs are publicly accessible while hosted. Website deployment and delivery use GitHub, Porkbun and Cloudflare, which can process website access requests under their own policies. OAuth tokens and app secrets are not included in these public files or the website repository.

Retention and control

Local queue data stays until the operator removes it. Hosted photos stay until the operator removes the deployed files; cached copies may require separate invalidation. There is no automatic deletion promise. The owner can revoke the application’s access using TikTok’s connected-app controls and can remove local authorization records or the complete local queue directory. Revoking access does not itself delete an already published TikTok post.

Contact

For access, deletion or privacy questions, contact support@twilock.com.
